properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 31 at 10:46AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Persistent northeast winds and downstream tidal effects on the St
John River have slowed flow at Astor. Forecast rainfall may lead to
additional rises within Moderate flood stage.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog and Bonnet roads become inaccessible with several
inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at
Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged.
Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards
completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded
in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno
Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 AM EDT Saturday the stage was 3.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:30 AM EDT Saturday was 3.7 feet.
- Forecast...Forecast rainfall may lead to additional rises within
Moderate Flood Stage.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1145 PM EDT.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 31 at 6:07AM MST until October 31 at 12:15PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Gila County in east central Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1215 PM MST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of Tonto Creek and flood-prone locations is
imminent or occurring. Tonto Creek continues to rise due to excess
runoff from earlier rainfall. Low-water crossings are inundated
with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 607 AM MST, a streamflow gauge on Tonto Creek north of Tonto
Basin rose above action stage, with a stage height of 5.12 feet
and flow of 2422 cfs as of 515 AM MST. Flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly along Tonto Creek in the warned area.
Please use the Tonto Creek Bridge for all travel across the
creek. Bar X Crossing, and any other low water crossings, will
likely become impassable.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Tonto Basin.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.description:

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...

- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:

Advisory for the following rivers in New Mexico...

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...San Francisco River at Reserve.

* WHEN...Rises on the river are expected to begin Sunday night and
last through Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 13.0 feet, Bankfull stage. Some minor overbank flow
may begin into drainage ditches near Highway 12.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:55 AM MDT Friday the stage was 10.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 13.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 13.0 feet
Monday morning.
- Action stage is 13.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

the possibility of the advisory being upgraded to a warning.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.
